title: Gröbner Basis Attack Bounds for Friday, Vision, RAIN, and Biscuit
summary: Same-scale random quadratic systems provide lower-bound intuition, but better upper and lower bounds for attacks on Friday, Vision, RAIN, and Biscuit remain open.

formal_statement.body: For the ciphers Friday, Vision, RAIN, and Biscuit, develop methods based on the overdefined-system-of-quadratic-equations modelling approach that more accurately estimate both upper and lower bounds for Gr?bner basis attack complexity. The constructed systems are not semi-regular, so semi-regularity-based reasoning cannot justify upper bounds, and solving a random quadratic system of the same scale provides only lower-bound intuition; the desired estimates must therefore account for the specific non-semi-regular systems of these four ciphers.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of Friday, Vision, RAIN, and Biscuit using overdefined systems of quadratic equations.
assumptions: The constructed quadratic systems are non-semi-regular.
parameters: System scale, used to match random quadratic systems to the modeled cipher systems for lower-bound estimation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Obtain more accurate upper and lower bounds for Gröbner basis attack complexity that account for the specific non-semi-regular systems of the four ciphers.

citations.label: Modelling Ciphers with Overdefined Systems of Quadratic Equations: Application to Friday, Vision, RAIN and Biscuit

progress.summary: The source treats solving a same-scale random quadratic system as a lower-bound reference. It explicitly leaves better estimation of both upper and lower bounds from the modelling method as an open problem.
citation_labels: Fukang Liu et al., Modelling Ciphers with Overdefined Systems of Quadratic Equations: Application to Friday, Vision, RAIN and Biscuit
